answer:
Python 3.9 has been deprecated, but the excerpts don't say it has been removed. The March 2026 changelog entries all carry the same line, for example: "chore: deprecate python 3.9 once and for all ([#20956](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/pull/20956))" [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/CHANGELOG.md]. That entry appears under llama-index-instrumentation 0.5.0 and llama-index-embeddings-litellm 0.5.0, among others, and PR #20956 is the common change.

The only "dropped" line I found refers to Python 3.8, not 3.9: "Dropped python3.8 support, Unpinned numpy (#16973)" [llama_index/docs/src/content/docs/framework/CHANGELOG.md], under llama-index-core 0.12.0 (2024-11-17).

I don't know whether 3.9 is now unsupported in installation requirements, or when it will be removed. The excerpts are partial and don't include the packages' Python version constraints.
